ORANDUM ON PROPERTY PURCHASE FOR A COLLEGE BUILDING TO REPLACE RENTED FACILITIES: 


At the close of World War II, the Federal Government set up a 
comprehensive scheme for demobilization and rehabilitation of Canada's Armed Forces. As 
a part of this plan, the Sir George Williams College was called upon to play a significant 
role in providing formal education for Veterans financed by the Department of Veterans 
Affairs student grants. At that time, it became necessary to expand the College facilities 
and consequently the Orphanage on Claremont Avenue and the Spanish Portugese Synagogue 
on Stanley Street were leased to provide additional class room accommodation. Some 
consideration was then given to the construction of a new College building, but it was 
felt that when the DVA program was completed, the College registration would not justify 
an expansion project of this nature, 

The Planning Committee of the Board of Governors of the Sir 
George Williams College, therefore, over an extended period has made an extensive study 
of the growth of the registration in the College and Schools, the nature of the student 
body, geographic distribution of the student body, the use of classrooms and other facilities 
in the present plant, the growing enrollment of students in the secondary schools of the 
province and the enrollment and possible plans of other institutions of higher learning 
in the city. 

Certain conclusions developed as a result of a study of this 
material which were reviewed and approved in general by the Survey Committee: 

(1) That current educational trends and the continued growth 
of the College especially in the last two years when veteran enrollment is decreasing, 
indicates that the College can plan confidently for a registration at least as large as 
at present and a great deal larger in the evening division if it wishes to permit growth 
6o continue. See schedule A, B, C and De 

(2) That present plant and facilities are being overworked and 
do not provide for the type of expansion and improvements which are obviously to be 
desired in the light of (1) above and that new or additional facilities ws 


necessary. 


é & 6 

(3) That the geographic distribution of the student body, in 
terms of residence and employment indicates that the College should be located in a 
downtown location. See Schedule E and Schedule F, 

(4) That economy of operation can best be assured if whatever 
new plant is provided is close enough to the present Central Building to allow for common 
heating plants and maintenance staff, 

(5) That some of the facilities now in use by the College in 
the Central Building could continue to be used, if necessary, provided they were not needed 
by Central Branch for its own purpose. 


The space now in use by the College and Schools is as follows: 


Central Branch Building 32,000 sq.ft. 
Stanley Street Annex Synagogue 11,808 sq.ft. 
Drummond Street Annex (Art School) #1 2,050 sqefte 
Drummond Street Annex #2 3,200 sq.fte 
Colley Hall(Salvation Army) 1,500 sq.ft. 
POTAL 50,558 square feet, 


The Planning Committee at the request of the Survey Committee 
proceeded further with the development of a space budget adequate to provide facilities for 
an evening enrollment of 6000 students, a conservative estimate of potential growth of the 
Colleges 

This space budget of 1,500,000 cubic feet was referred to the 
YMCA Building Bureau for detailed study in relation to property available in the Drummond 
Stanley Street area. Various schemes were examined and studied, having in mind that the 
College expansion would be a major factor but not the only project in any total YMCA scheme 
involving other branches and districts. After a careful review of all aspects of the 
problem, it was apparent that the minimum need would be a College building to replace vented 
facilities in the Stanley Street Synagogue, Drimmond Street Annexes and Colley Hall (Salvation 


Army). While this suggestion would provide little if any expanded facilities, it would 


- 3 « 
nevertheless stabilize the current academic program of the College and reduce administrative 
problems by consolidating the varied activities carried on in four buildings in one new 
building adjacent, if possible to the present Central Branch building. 

It was soon evident that the major problem at this stage of the 
study was to locate property within the immediate vicinity of the Y.M.C.A., adequate for 
such a building. Accordingly, investigations were carried on to ascertain the dimensions 
and probable costs of property at 131 Drummond Street, 1435 Drummond Street, 17-80 
Drummond Street, 3540 Drummond Street, 136 Stanley Street, 12 Stanley Street, and the 
entire area between the Synagogue and Burnside on the East side of Stanley Street. At 
various stages in these enquiries, the Building Bureau was asked to study the space budget 
of the College in relation to these available properties. The probable extension of 
Burnside Street West and the possibility that a strip of land on the North side of the 
Central Building would be available in the not too distant future, was also investigated 
and the data placed on file for future reference if necessary. 

After an exhaustive examination of all the possible alternatives, 
two facts seemed to emerge: (a) that the study cannot proceed further without the | 
acquisition of a specific piece of property, (b) the most desirable location is the 
properties located at 1431 Drummond Street, 135 Drummond Street and 1Wh2 Stanley Streets 

The Survey Committee therefore decided to ask the Finance and 
Property Committee to give consideration to the immediate purchase of these properties, 


the descriptions of which are as follows:

REMARKS: Servitude created on rear twelve feet of property to provide for lane. This would

In addition to the three properties described, the property located at 1436 
Stanley Street owned and operated by the Mount Bruno Floral Company may be available at some 
future date if the company can find suitable facilities elsewhere. This represents an area 
of 22'5" x 109' 6" or 2463 square feet. It has an assessed value of $22,000 and a probable 
purchase price at current levels of $50,000. Taxes are $723. See Schedule G for map of three 
areas indicated above, 

In summary, the three available properties, 1431 and 1435 Drummond Street and 
1442 Stanley Street, containing 13, 855 square feet with an assessed value of $103,500, can 
be purchased for $212,500, The current annual net revenue therefrom is approximately $13, 39, 

The Finance and Property Committee, after dealing with the subject generally, 
referred the matter to a special sub-committee for further study and data relative to the 


possible steps which might be taken in financing the transaction.
